subject: Forensic data access scope + retention (post-incident) — quick clarifications
messages:
From: Alex Norton <alex.norton@acmecloud.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: sec-ops@acmecloud.com
Date: Sat, 27 Mar 2027 14:23:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify log export scope and retention after last week's outage

Karthik / Marissa — thanks again for the quick coordination on Friday. Our forensics team needs a couple of clarifications before we begin ingesting the artifacts you shared. Please see the questions below; answers will help us scope our access and maintain chain-of-custody.

1) Exact retention window: you exported application and proxy logs for the 48-hour window around the incident. Can you confirm the start/end timestamps (UTC) that Redwood preserved?
2) Data residency: will the exported archives include any user PII that is EU/UK resident? If so, we need confirmation of where those archives will be stored while AcmeCloud processes them.
3) Access model: who at Redwood will have read access to the exported archive and for how long? We prefer a short allowlist and time-limited credentials.
4) Forensic completeness: were ephemeral debug traces, in-memory snippets, or kernel-level logs included, or is this strictly application + LB + auth logs?

If you can reply with answers or a short plan (who/where/when) that would be great — we aim to start analysis Monday morning PST.

Best,
Alex
Alex Norton
Sr. Security Engineer, AcmeCloud
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Norton <alex.norton@acmecloud.com>, sec-ops@acmecloud.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Mar 2027 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify log export scope and retention after last week's outage

Alex — thanks for the clear questions. Quick answers below; attaching the export manifest and C-of-C.

- Retention window: exported logs cover 2027-03-24T21:00:00Z through 2027-03-26T21:00:00Z (48 hours, UTC).
- Data residency: archive contains request metadata and user identifiers (hashed user_id). No raw billing/payment PII included. To our knowledge no EU/UK resident-specific fields are present, but we flagged records where geo-country header resolves to EU countries — those are included in a separate folder named eu_tagged/ inside the archive.
- Access model: read access is restricted to the Redwood incident response group (Marissa, Mina, Karthik) by default. We will provision a pre-signed, time-limited S3 URL valid for 72 hours and provide one-time credentials for AcmeCloud's forensics engineers; access will be logged and recorded.
- Forensic completeness: export includes application logs, load-balancer logs, auth events, and our dd-kernel crash dumps where existent. It does not include full in-memory heap snapshots or container local disks beyond log rotations.

Attachments: forensic-log-export-manifest.txt, chain-of-custody_acme_redwood_20270328.pdf

If you need more granular retention (e.g., longer than 72 hours), we can arrange a staged handoff to your secure bucket with signed ACLs for 14 days — will need an MOU.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales (Enterprise), Redwood Inference
From: Ben Jones <ben.jones@pacifica.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Norton <alex.norton@acmecloud.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify log export scope and retention after last week's outage

Karthik / team — quick note from the forensics side: a couple of practical asks to avoid rework on our end.

- Please ensure the exported logs include original ingestion timestamps (not just processing timestamps) — we need event-time ordering.
- If possible, include a checksum (SHA256) per archive file and the manifest listed in the C-of-C PDF.
- For the eu_tagged/ folder: can you mark which fields triggered the EU tag (country header vs IP geolocation) so we can apply the right privacy handling?

Also: would Redwood accept a short read-only account in your audit trail system so our engineers can pull logs directly rather than downloading the entire zip? That reduces duplication and shortens turnaround.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Jones
Forensics Lead, Pacifica (third-party retained by AcmeCloud)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Jones <ben.jones@pacifica.com>, Alex Norton <alex.norton@acmecloud.com>, sec-ops@acmecloud.com
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify log export scope and retention after last week's outage

Ben / Alex — thanks. Quick replies inline: 

- Ingestion timestamps: yes, original event_time (ISO) is preserved in each log line — we'll include a small mapping doc in the manifest explaining fields.
- Checksums: will add SHA256 checksums to the manifest; already computing now.
- EU tagging: the eu_tagged/ folder is populated based on the 'CF-IPCountry' header first; we fallback to MaxMind IP lookup only where the header is absent. We'll annotate which method was used per-file in manifest.
- Read-only audit account: we can provision a scoped, short-lived viewer role in our audit system (token valid 48 hours) so your team can query traces directly. That requires an NDA addendum for cross-company audit access — legal has a one-page.

Proposed next steps:
- We will publish pre-signed S3 URL + manifest + checksums by 2027-03-29T13:00:00Z.
- AcmeCloud/Pacifica to confirm desired access window (72h default) or request extended retention with MOU.
- If your team wants the read-only token, sign the addendum and send the account list (name + email) for allowlist.

Attachments referenced: forensic-log-export-20270327.zip (staged), chain-of-custody_acme_redwood_20270328.pdf

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Trust & Security, Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alex Norton <alex.norton@acmecloud.com>, Ben Jones <ben.jones@pacifica.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify log export scope and retention after last week's outage

Alex / Ben — confirming handoff plan and a few operational notes:

- S3 pre-signed URL (read-only) will be shared via secure DocuSign link by 2027-03-30T14:00:00Z. URL TTL: 72 hours.
- We will enable object-level access logs for the bucket and provide the first 7 days of those logs to AcmeCloud as part of the C-of-C package.
- Access allowlist: Ben Jones <ben.jones@pacifica.com>, Alex Norton <alex.norton@acmecloud.com>. If you need additional users, please reply with full names and emails.
- Extended retention: for anything >72 hours we require a signed MOU (template attached) and will move the artifacts to your secure bucket with ACLs.

Note: chain-of-custody PDF attached includes who handled the export and an MD5/SHA256 manifest summary. If you want a notarized copy we can escalate.

Please confirm you have everything you need to begin analysis.

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Incident Response Manager, Redwood Inference
